_about: Abraham Kuyper (1837-1920) in English, the works not on the abraham-kuyper shelf (draft PR #14): the 1895 Calvinism, the Origin and Safeguard of our Constitutional Liberties, his Philadelphia lecture The Antithesis between Symbolism and Revelation, The South-African Crisis (1900, tr. A. E. Fletcher) and J. H. de Vries's two 1929 meditation volumes, Asleep in Jesus and In the Shadow of Death. A gaps shelf, after the chesterton-gaps precedent, so as not to edit another thread's shelf. Texts are from Internet Archive scans; every printing is 1929 or earlier, so public domain in the US. Added 2026-10-28 by lane A at Adam's request (his Reformed authors table). No uids minted.

kuyper-calvinism-liberties-1895: Calvinism: the origin and safeguard of our constitutional liberties (1895)
kuyper-south-african-crisis-1900: The South-African crisis, reprinted from the Revue des Deux Mondes for February 1900, translated and prefaced by A. E. Fletcher, fourth edition (London: Stop the War Committee, 1900)
kuyper-asleep-in-jesus-1929: Asleep in Jesus: meditations, tr. J. H. de Vries (Grand Rapids: Eerdmans, 1929)
kuyper-shadow-of-death-1929: In the shadow of death: meditations for the sick-room and at the death-bed, tr. J. H. de Vries (Grand Rapids: Eerdmans, 1929)
kuyper-antithesis-lecture: The antithesis between symbolism and revelation: lecture delivered before the Historical Presbyterian Society in Philadelphia (Amsterdam and Pretoria: Höveker & Wormser; Edinburgh: T. & T. Clark; undated printing, catalogued 1857)

_excluded.kuyper-dutch: Dutch-language works (De twaalf patriarchen, Het werk van den Heiligen Geest, Gedenkboek) and the a Lasco Opera he edited
_excluded.kuyper-dups: other scans and later printings of the books on the abraham-kuyper shelf
_excluded.kuyper-later: Women of the Old Testament, The Revelation of St. John, The Practice of Godliness and other translations printed after 1929

_rights_checked.kuyper-antithesis-lecture: Undated. The catalogue's 1857 cannot be right: the title page styles him LL.D. and M.P., and his LL.D. was Princeton's of 1898 (stated in the preface to The South-African Crisis on this shelf). A printing in his lifetime (he died 1920), so before 1930 and US public domain. Read 2026-10-28.
